report: Done: I investigated KrownJM's voice latency and changed nothing. The capture and speech code runs on his PC in the Java client mod (`client-mod/`), so the box can't time it, and this shell can't run the Python measurement tools. From the repo's measured numbers, the mod's defaults give a median of 0.49 s from his last word to the line being ready: a 0.35 s Silero VAD pause, then Parakeet transcription and a roughly 35 ms Smart Turn score, which decides whether the line closes at once or waits up to 3 s. That probably accounts for most of his 0.6 s. On the box, a voice line waits at most 50 ms, action and conversational lines skip the batch wait, then Jev classifies it and the brain answers. The box log shows about 4 s from one of his lines to the AI's acknowledgement (06:20:33 to 06:20:37), so the server side is probably the bigger share, but Jev's and the brain's own times aren't measured here. The trade-offs: cutting the VAD pause to about 0.2 s saves roughly 0.15 s but risks splitting sentences, and needs a client rebuild on his PC; lowering the turn threshold to 0.35 (turn-1-mini) cuts off unfinished speech more often and doesn't clearly help; Moonshine tiny is faster but makes more errors than Parakeet (19.2% against 11.5% word errors for base). Recognition errors matter more than 0.6 s: his casts came through as "Hot fire bowl", "Tijum", "Hawfio" and "Destroying every bin". Skipping Jev for lines that match an incantation would save one API round-trip, at the cost of its context. Before any change, run `./gradlew speechTest` on his PC and time Jev and the brain from the box logs; any change to the client or the server waits for the brain's go-ahead.

report: Done, with a caveat: I could not run new benchmarks from this shell (it refuses Gradle, Java and Python measurement tools), so every number below comes from the repo's own reports, measured on the owner's PC on 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-10. The main finding is that the 0.6 s is not the main latency problem. A line closes at once when Smart Turn scores it finished, but on Kokoro-spoken game asks it scores 19% of finished asks unfinished, and those wait the full 3 s silence timeout, so the average is pulled up by about 0.6 s. Lowering the Smart Turn threshold to 0.3 cuts that wait to 15% but cuts off 35% of unfinished asks mid-sentence. Asking the model 0.6 s into the pause, rather than 0.2 s, cuts those waits from 5.4% to 1.5% on the public set, but adds 0.4 s to every line, which is a net loss. turn-1-mini is worse on both counts: it keeps 64% of game asks waiting at its chosen 0.35 threshold. On recognition, Parakeet TDT 110M (the current default) makes 11.5% word errors against Moonshine base's 19.2% on Minecraft-heavy speech, at similar size, speed and memory; the repo's hotwords option for Parakeet is experimental and was not benchmarked against the errors seen in the log ("Hot fire bowl", "Tijum", "Hawfio"). The cheapest accuracy fix is the incantation aliases the keyword spotter already supports. Streaming recognition (partial text during speech, so nothing is left to transcribe after the pause) and a sherpa streaming model are plausible next steps, but they are not in the repo and would need a sttCompare run before any recommendation. Server-side time (the Jev filter, then the brain) is also unmeasured: the box logs show about 4 s from one of his lines to the AI's acknowledgement. My recommendation: keep Parakeet and Smart Turn at 0.5, measure the hotwords and a streaming model with `./gradlew sttCompare` and `micCheck` on the owner's PC, and time Jev and the brain from the box logs before changing any threshold. No changes were made to the game or the code.
